title: A Hormone Cell Atlas maps the human endocrine system at cellular resolution.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Opened four small tables from hormonecellatlas.org.uk/accounts/downloads: Table S1A (171 rows: study per tissue, with GEO accessions, donor counts, sex/age/BMI groups), S2C (about 388 endocrine genes with category and include/exclude status), S2D (hormone-producing cell definitions: 1-8 marker genes per hormone), S2E (hormone-receiving definitions: receptor genes per hormone). HEAD on the per-tissue h5ad (AnnData single-cell files): Adipose 3.66 GB, Blood 2.96 GB, Pituitary 348 MB, Thyroid 134 MB; 47 tissues are listed, plus CellTypist cell-type classifier bundles. The Science supplement zip returned 403. The PMC ID that NCBI links to (PMC13278015) is a different paper (PanKbase islet atlas), not this one.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 14 million cells, 47 tissues, 379 hormone and receptor genes, and the hormone2cell scoring method come from the abstract and the site's About page; no full text was available. I did not open any h5ad, so per-tissue cell counts are unverified.

a1_downloadable.note: h5ad files and small tables download without login (checked with HEAD and real downloads); the Science supplement zip is blocked (403).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The atlas's new outputs, hormone-producing and hormone-receiving cell scores, are not measured labels; they would have to be rebuilt by applying the hormone2cell rules to the expression matrix. The only ready-made per-cell column is the cell-type annotation.

a3_inputs_present.note: Expression matrices are inside the h5ad files (seen only through HEAD; not opened).

a4_units_stated.note: Not relevant for count matrices; not checked inside the files.

a5_enough_rows.note: The paper claims 14M cells; not counted. At the level of donors or studies the real unit is about 171 study-tissue entries (Table S1A).

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Several GB per large tissue (Adipose 3.66 GB, Blood 2.96 GB); the full atlas is likely tens of GB
a6_fits_laptop.note: Single small tissues fit; the cross-tissue task the atlas is built for does not fit without heavy subsetting.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 47 tissues on the download page matches the abstract; cell counts not verified.

a8_label_provenance.note: Circular. The hormone-producing and hormone-receiving scores are computed from the expression of the marker and receptor genes listed in Tables S2D and S2E, so a model predicting them from expression only learns the scoring formula. Cell-type labels come from author annotation, and the authors already release CellTypist models for them.

existing_models.name: CellTypist models released by the authors (47 tissues, level 1 and level 2 cell types)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not reported on the download page; not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: The About page says the scores are transcript-based and putative, and need functional validation.

integration.partner_dataset: Genomics England PanelApp (already used by the authors), GTEx
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: None that avoids reusing the expression-derived scores as labels.

controls.positive_control: Classical endocrine cells (pituitary corticotrophs producing POMC, thyroid follicular cells producing TG) should score as hormone-producing.
controls.external_validation: None with a measured hormone secretion label

honest_claim_h3: A model could only reproduce the hormone2cell rule-based expression scores; it could not claim to predict actual hormone secretion or response.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use single-cell gene expression to predict which cell types make or respond to each hormone across human tissues.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-cell expression profiles from 47 tissues (14M cells claimed; not counted).
plain_idea.predict: Hormone-producing and hormone-receiving scores, which the authors compute from the expression of listed marker and receptor genes, so they are not measured outcomes.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Endocrinologists could find unexpected sites where hormones are made, but the labels add nothing that the authors' scoring rule doesn't already give.

ml_idea: Predict hormone-producing or receiving status per cell type from expression. Rejected because the labels are a deterministic function of the input genes.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because the project was rejected at Part A; file sizes come from HEAD requests.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read Table S2D: hormone-producing status is defined by marker-gene expression, so it is circular.

verdict_reason: Fails A8 and A2: the atlas's hormone-producing and hormone-receiving labels are computed from the expression of marker and receptor genes listed in Tables S2D and S2E, so predicting them from expression is circular. The only measured-style label, cell type, already has released CellTypist models. Large tissues are also 3-4 GB each (A6).
